test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 23 Oct, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution has provisions for the appointment of High Court Judges?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 217**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 217 of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with the **appointment and conditions of the office of High Court Judges**.
 
• The President of India appoints High Court Judges after consultation with the **Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the respective state, and the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court**.
 
• A person is qualified for appointment as a High Court Judge if they have served as an advocate in a High Court for at least **10 years** or have held judicial office in India for the same duration.
 
• The retirement age of a High Court Judge is **62 years**, as per the provisions under Article 217.
 
• The procedure for removal of High Court Judges is the same as for Supreme Court Judges and is governed by **Article 124(4) of the Constitution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Court in India:**

 
 
• Each state in India has its own High Court, which acts as the highest judicial authority within the state.
 
• The High Court has original, appellate, and writ jurisdiction under the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Collegium System:**
 
 
• The appointment of High Court Judges involves the **Collegium System**, where senior judges of the Supreme Court recommend names to the President.
 
• This system ensures judicial independence and transparency.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• High Courts have the power of judicial review under Article 226, enabling them to examine the constitutionality of laws and executive actions.
 
• This is a crucial function to uphold the principles of justice and the rule of law.
 
 
 
• **Removal of Judges:**
 
 
• High Court Judges can be removed only through impeachment by Parliament, as per the procedure outlined in the Judges Inquiry Act, 1968.
 
• This ensures that removal is not arbitrary and is conducted with due process.
